objective: Build MAGIC DECK LAB inside Brain: a production-usable, GENERAL-PURPOSE mathematical Magic: The Gathering deck-design system for Commander and Standard, plus a pre-populated Precon Commander League workspace that is ALREADY PRESENT on the owner's first visit. Source: 'Brain / Magic Deck Lab Implementation Specification' (2026-10-31). The general deck engine is the primary product; the league is one saved workspace of the SAME engine, never the architecture other decks are rewritten around. Implement working software, durable state, tests and production integration; a plan, mock-up or static dashboard is not completion. FOLLOW CLAUDE.md: extend existing owners (React/Vite client with client/src/lib/router.ts and client/src/russell/RussellShell.tsx, Express routes behind the existing guard and services/identity/policy.ts via requireProject/requirePerson resolvers, repos over the async Database adapter, numbered SQLite + Postgres migrations, Vitest). No second frontend, standalone service, scheduler, queue, auth mechanism or scenario framework. No paid APIs and no AI-invented card text, rules, combos, prices, legalities or win probabilities. MODULES (architect splits into units with disjoint owned paths; schema first, then catalog/rules, then engine/optimizer, league, UI, integration): (1) NAVIGATION: a secondary 'Magic' (Deck Lab) entry in the Russell shell's More menu, bookmarkable reloadable /magic with subsections Design, My Decks, Optimize, Matchups, League, Collection, Exports; mobile usable; does not displace the six primary destinations (CLAUDE.md 57). First entry offers: describe a new deck, import a deck, optimize a saved deck, open the Precon Commander League. (2) CARD CATALOG: canonical cards keyed by Scryfall Oracle ID with separate printings (set, collector number, prices, image URIs), faces, types, mana cost, color identity, legalities, rulings. Discover the current bulk file at runtime from https://api.scryfall.com/bulk-data (never hard-code a download URI), stream/process it bounded and cancellably off the request path, keep per-source fetch timestamps, serve the cached index on outage and label it stale. One shared catalog, not per account. Handle double-faced/modal cards, partner/background, alternate names and rules exceptions (e.g. Relentless Rats, Persistent Petitioners, any-number cards) by verified rules data, not loose string matching. Tests use committed fixtures, never the network. (3) FORMAT RULES (one engine, separate rule sets): Commander = exactly 100 including commander(s), color identity, singleton except basic lands and printed exceptions, ban list, valid partner/background pairs; changing commander revalidates the whole deck. Standard = 60+ main, max 4 copies except basics/exceptions, current legality as of analysis date, sideboard <= 15. POST /api/magic/validate. (4) DECK STORE: magic_decks with append-only magic_deck_versions (current pointer to newest selected version), cards per version with zone commander/main/sideboard, undo to prior version, version diff (explicit add/cut), plaintext import (count + name, sections commander/main/sideboard) surfacing unknown/ambiguous names and printings explicitly, plaintext export. Collection (owned vs proxy) stored separately from deck membership. Owner-scoped; cross-user reads/writes refused with the same 404 body as absent (invariant 23). (5) STRATEGY ARCHITECT (structured, deterministic; may use Brain's existing assistant interface for explanation only if available, never a fake AI button): turn a rough idea (e.g. 'extremely defensive Commander deck, lots of ways to stop threats, lifegain, but able to finish games quickly') into structured fields: format, primary outcome, win engines, secondary preferences, hard constraints vs adjustable weights, risk/consistency priority, collection, budget, opponents, playstyle. Detect incompatible goals (e.g. defensive with no closing path, high curve with no early mana), explain the cost, offer 2-3 coherent alternative builds with tradeoffs, ask at most ONE decision when it changes the next step, otherwise proceed with explicit provisional assumptions; iterative refinement; supported archetypes include aggro, control, midrange, tempo, combo, defensive, political multiplayer, go-wide, sacrifice, recursion, life-drain, tribal, artifacts, budget, custom. Build real cards only after strategy and constraints are coherent, from the catalog. (6) ANALYSIS ENGINE (deterministic, code-first): exact hypergeometric P(at least one) = 1 - C(N-K,n)/C(N,n) with BigInt/exact rationals, multivariate/joint events for overlapping categories (never add percentages; one card never counted as two draws), command zone separate from the 99-card library, lands/ramp/draw/answers/engines by turn, colored-source castability (correct untapped sources when castable), mana curve, color distribution, opening-hand ranges and mulligans, threats answered by type, redundancy, sweep resilience, single-card reliance, closing ability in 1v1. Tags from oracle data plus curated machine-testable rules; AI-derived tags are proposals until checked. Monte Carlo uses seeded reproducible streams and reports runs, assumptions, mulligan policy, draw rules and confidence intervals. Every number is labelled EXACT_PROBABILITY, MODEL_ESTIMATE, HEURISTIC_SCORE or EMPIRICAL_MATCH_RESULT; a composite score is never shown as a win rate. POST /api/magic/analyze. (7) OPTIMIZER: multi-objective constrained search (beam search plus local swaps, or equivalent) over real add/cut packages and whole decks; a candidate violating construction rules, protected cards, identity, price ceiling, exclusions or collection limits is invalid before scoring; score vector (consistency, early development, threats answered, survival, independent closing, points potential, price, preference match) with components, uncertainty and tradeoffs; compare to the unchanged baseline; keep a Pareto frontier of non-dominated builds with adjustable weights; rank upgrades by objective gain per dollar without forcing full budget spend. POST /api/magic/optimize. (8) PRICES: per exact printing MARKET price with source, timestamp and CONFIRMED/ESTIMATE status; a Scryfall price is an ESTIMATE, not a verified TCGplayer market price; user may enter a shop/league-verified price with date/source and lock a snapshot; surface ambiguity rather than inventing; alternate printings with delta; USD integer-cent math with exact 9.99/10.00/10.01 boundaries; no purchasing automation. (9) LEAGUE WORKSPACE, seeded idempotently in the OWNER's scope on first access, never overwriting edits, never asking for these facts: league 'Precon Commander League'; owner deck CHAOS INCARNATE, commander KARDUR, DOOMSCOURGE, original unmodified 2022 Starter Commander precon, loaded as its exact verified official 100-card list (cite official source and date in the seed; earlier discussed $10 lists are suggestions only, not purchases). Six OTHER participant records exactly: 1 'Red Foundations' (label confirmed; product/commander/list UNKNOWN; do not invent Reign of Dragons or any list); 2 'Other Chaos Incarnate (provisional)' (probably another Chaos Incarnate player; unverified, editable); 3 'Sky Warden / First Flight' (2022 First Flight stock 99 when officially verified; player is CHANGING COMMANDER not deck; replacement commander UNKNOWN; keep prior commander and candidate context separate; revalidate the 99 when the change is confirmed); 4 'Undead Girl / Grave Danger' (2022 Grave Danger, Gisa and Geralf; observed noncombat life drain of roughly 3/6/9 per turn without attacks; causing card(s) NOT confirmed; do not invent purchases or trigger identity); 5 'Green Foundations' (product/commander/list UNKNOWN; observed many creatures, which made Kardur's goad useful; do not invent Tramplesaurus Rex or any list); 6 'Token Triumph' (2022 Emmara deck; load validated official 100). Known official precon lists are loaded ONLY when they validate to 100 with source and date; unknown decks stay named records labelled 'unverified cardlist'. Rules: pods usually 4 (configurable), 40 life, $10 market value of singles EACH WEEK OR a permitted option of two booster packs (user-described as 5/8 packs; exact sets pending confirmation and never blocking singles), pack purchases tracked separately from singles, rollover NOT confirmed (assume none, visibly pending and editable, never accumulate unconfirmed money), date-locked weekly ledger of verified add/cut with printing, value and before/after deck version; suggested cards are not purchases; proxies cannot evade the budget. Scoring: credited eliminations 1 point for each of the first two and 2 for the final elimination; points go to the player whose OWN spell, creature or ability causes the elimination; Kardur's own life-loss trigger earns points; Kardur forcing opponent A to attack and kill B does NOT earn the Kardur player that kill (the attacker's controller is credited); simultaneous elimination, commander damage and alternate losses are editable house rules, never silently assigned. In 1v1 Kardur's goad is weak/harmful and attack-only defenses do nothing against noncombat drain. (10) MATCHUPS: environment of known opponents/deck versions/pod mixes; target is EXPECTED LEAGUE POINTS per game with first/second/final logic and opponent point denial, not raw win rate; opponent upgrade predictor produces uncertainty-weighted HYPOTHESES never shown as confirmed purchases; manual observations of revealed cards, commanders, purchases and results update opponent versions while preserving historical snapshots (unknown First Flight replacement commander stays UNKNOWN until observed); match log with date, 3 opponents and their deck versions/commanders, turn, life snapshots, key cards, threats, eliminations with source/controller attribution, points for all players, outcome and notes; empirical points/win rates by matchup with game counts and intervals. ENDPOINTS: /api/magic/decks/*, /api/magic/design/*, /api/magic/analyze, /api/magic/optimize, /api/magic/validate, /api/magic/leagues/*, /api/magic/catalog/*, /api/magic/prices/*. STORAGE (names consistent with repo conventions; both migration chains; applied files never edited; history sufficient to replay prior deck/league state): magic_cards, magic_printings, magic_decks, magic_deck_versions, magic_deck_cards, magic_design_intents, magic_analyses, magic_collections, magic_leagues, magic_league_rules, magic_league_players, magic_league_decks, magic_weekly_ledgers, magic_purchases, magic_price_snapshots, magic_games, magic_game_participants, magic_eliminations, magic_observations. Document the feature in docs/MAGIC.md. API/network failures show recoverable errors and stale-cache labels, never silent green results.
expectedOutcome: A signed-in person opens Brain, goes to More -> Magic (/magic), describes an incomplete or contradictory deck idea, negotiates the tradeoff, receives a legal evidence-backed Commander or Standard deck, saves, versions, analyzes, optimizes and exports it; and on first visit finds the Precon Commander League already seeded (Chaos Incarnate / Kardur 100, six opponent records with honest unknowns, $10 weekly rule, booster option, 1/1/2 scoring) with persistent match and upgrade history, all deterministic, owner-scoped and covered by the acceptance journeys.
nonGoals: A standalone app, second frontend, separately hosted demo, or new scheduler/queue/auth/scenario framework beside Brain's existing owners.
Paid APIs, purchasing automation, or scraping TCGplayer; a Scryfall price is never presented as a verified TCGplayer market price.
Invented card text, rules, combos, decklists, prices, legalities, purchases or win probabilities; a composite score shown as a win rate.
Inventing lists for Red Foundations, Green Foundations, the unknown First Flight replacement commander, or the Grave Danger drain source.
A full multiplayer rules engine or accurate predicted opponent purchases presented as such.
A setup wizard asking the owner to type league facts already supplied.
Displacing Brain's six primary destinations, or changing authorization policy, identity, deployment workflows or cash/research/orchestration systems.
Hard-coding a stale Scryfall bulk download URI, or fetching the network inside tests.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 1: from the Brain shell, More -> Magic -> Design; a rough contradictory idea (extremely defensive + lifegain + fast win) yields a concrete tradeoff proposal with 2-3 alternatives, accepts priorities, generates a VALID 100-card Commander deck from catalog cards, explains card roles, saves and exports it.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest integration test driving the routes (and a client test of the Magic page) over a fixture catalog; asserts validation passes at exactly 100 with color identity and singleton respected, a version row exists, and the export round-trips through import.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 2: importing a Standard list validates legality, copy counts and sideboard as of an analysis date, evaluates, optimizes within a budget, saves a new version and shows the exact add/cut diff; reload persists.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest: import with an unknown name and an over-4 copy is reported explicitly; optimize under a price ceiling returns a diff; a fresh read returns the same versions.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 3: the first League request immediately returns 'Precon Commander League' with Chaos Incarnate/Kardur at 100 validated cards, exactly six opponent records with the stated labels and UNKNOWN/provisional flags, the $10 weekly allowance, booster option, 1/1/2 rule and unresolved commander/Foundations/rollover fields; repeated access or a second session never duplicates the league or erases edits.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest calling the league route twice and after an edit, on both SQLite and Postgres; row counts unchanged and the edit preserved.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 4: evaluating the next $10 ranks real card swaps using exact-print prices, flags unverified (estimate) prices, refuses approval above $10.00, and price math is exact at 9.99, 10.00 and 10.01.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest boundary tests on integer-cent math and the eligibility gate; an ESTIMATE price cannot be marked league-approved.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 5: testing a different commander against the same base 99 recalculates legality; Kardur's goad is not counted as protection in 1v1 while his own life-loss ability is valued; Grave Danger noncombat drain is not treated as stopped by attack-only defenses.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest on the analysis/matchup engine with the seeded decks.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 6: recording a four-player game where opponent A's goaded attack eliminates B (0 to the Kardur player), Kardur's trigger eliminates C (1 point) and the owner's spell eliminates the final opponent (2 points) scores the owner 3, not 4, and the game log and every player's credits persist.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest through /api/magic/leagues routes asserting stored eliminations, attribution and standings.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 7: recording a revealed alternate First Flight commander and a newly observed Zombie card creates a new opponent version and updated matchup evaluation without mutating the precon baseline or marking predicted purchases as facts.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest asserting the baseline version is unchanged and the hypothesis/observation labels.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Journey 8: hypergeometric results match independent exact values (e.g. 99-card library, 37 lands, 7 cards), joint events do not double count, seeded Monte Carlo reproduces identical results with the same seed, colored-mana castability and singleton/identity rules are correct, and the optimizer reports its comparison to the unchanged baseline.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest unit tests with hand-computed expected values and seed reproducibility.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Data is owner-scoped: an authenticated second user cannot read or write the owner's decks or league, and the refusal body equals that of a non-existent id.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest HTTP test with two principals comparing response bodies byte for byte.

acceptanceConditions.statement: The catalog discovers the bulk file from the bulk-data manifest at runtime, processes it bounded off the request path, records fetch timestamps, and on fetch failure keeps serving the cached index labelled stale; the UI shows recoverable errors rather than silent green results.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Vitest with a stubbed fetch returning a manifest, then an outage; no real network in tests.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Mobile navigation reaches /magic and its subsections; every visible button performs its action; reload of /magic and its subsection URLs restores the view.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Client Vitest (jsdom) over RussellShell routing and the Magic page controls.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Migrations exist in both server/db/migrations and server/db/pg-migrations, boot from an empty database and restart against an existing one, and the full typecheck and impacted tests pass.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm run typecheck && npm run test:impacted (and npm run test:pg for persistence).

rollbackRequirement: Revert the merged pull request. Migrations only add new magic_* tables; no existing table or row changes meaning, so removing the feature leaves every other Brain system as it was.
